source.title: PowLU: An Activation Function for Stable Pre-Training of LLMs
source.authors: Peijie Jiang; Yuqi Feng; Cunyin Peng; Qian Zhao; Jia Liu; KunLong Chen; Zhiqiang Zhang; Jun Zhou

record.tranche_reason: It runs a model-size scaling sweep and reports fitted loss-scaling curves, using the same broad loss-versus-parameter-count measurement as the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports scaling curves for SwiGLU and PowLU. Its 7.9B and 124B benchmark comparisons, loss-spike analysis, tensor-distribution plots, and the single-size hyperparameter ablation do not test the claim's specified scaling relations or compute-optimal allocation, so they are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study runs a small scaling sweep (26M–368M activated parameters, about one order of magnitude) only to show PowLU matches SwiGLU. It reports no exponents, fit quality or check of the power-law form. Its result is about its own activation function's performance, not whether the scaling law holds.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that PowLU gives benchmark performance competitive with SwiGLU and SwiGLU-Clip at 7.9B and 124B, and improves training stability (fewer loss spikes and outliers). They describe the scaling-law sweep only as showing PowLU's performance is consistent with SwiGLU across sizes; they draw no conclusion about scaling laws themselves.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a Ling MoE size sweep and plots fitted loss-scaling curves for SwiGLU and PowLU. It does not specify the fitting procedure, a held-out evaluation measure, or a multi-axis parameter/token/compute sweep.

fits_no_version.finding: Swapping SwiGLU for PowLU barely changes the fitted loss-scaling curve across 26M–368M activated-parameter MoE models. At 47M, the loss difference is +0.002 (1.912 vs 1.910, Table 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-function choice (within gated variants) shifts the loss-vs-size scaling curve only negligibly.

record.problems: For the scaling result, the text gives no numerical curve values, fitted exponents, uncertainty estimates, or fitting procedure. It does not state whether the plotted loss is held-out, and the activated-parameter range is 26M to 368M.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 2 and 3 report downstream benchmark scores for 7.9B and 124B models, not scaling predictions. Section 4.3 and Figures 4–7 report stability, loss spikes, and tensor distributions rather than the claimed scaling relations. Table 4 reports a single-size loss comparison for the m ablation, not a scaling sweep.

untested.parts: Whether loss follows a power law in parameters, tokens or compute: the paper reports no fit parameters or deviations, the range is about one order of magnitude, and held-out status is not stated.
No small-run fit is used to predict the 7.9B or 124B runs.
No depth/width variation at fixed parameter count. Depth and width co-vary with size in Table 1.
No other modalities or training regimes.
Downstream benchmarks are reported at only two sizes, with different activations, and are not related to scale or loss.

record.verdict_notes: This is an activation-function paper. The 'scaling law experiments' are a comparison tool, and the reader's T1/tests classification and V1 limits_scope label overstate the relation. The fitted curves appear only in Figure 3, with no numbers in the text.

versions.untested_parts: The text does not state whether the loss is held-out; the experiment varies activated parameter count only, across 26M to 368M, and does not test token-count or compute scaling or a several-orders-of-magnitude range.
No small-run fit is reported as predicting much larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or parameter/token compute-optimal trend is reported.
No comparison holds parameter count fixed while varying depth, width, or other architecture details.
No other modalities, repeated-data training, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling experiments are reported.
Downstream benchmark scores are compared across activation functions, but their predictability from scale or pretraining loss is not tested.
The paper does not test sensitivity to fitting choices, compare published exponents, or report curves bending away from a power law.

rows.subject: MoE LLM scaling-law series
rows.operation_detail: Fit and plot loss-scaling curves across model sizes
rows.measure: Fitted loss-scaling curve versus activated parameter count; loss type and held-out status not stated
rows.note: The text says the SwiGLU and PowLU curves almost overlap and have roughly the same performance over the reported size range. The plotted values and fit details are not given in the text; this is the aggregate curve for the five model sizes.
rows.check: This row is the SwiGLU baseline in a comparison with the study's own method. It reports no exponent, fit quality or numeric loss values, so it cannot show whether loss follows a power law. The 26M–368M range spans about one order of magnitude, and held-out status is not stated. The 'partial' state was inferred from an overlap statement that bears on PowLU vs SwiGLU, not on V1.
